commitResults.messageTitle: feat: add Maple greeting and exit flow
docs: rename project references to Maple
feat: echo user commands and exit on 'bye'
commitResults.messageBody:
Read each line of input and echo it back framed by separators.
Terminate the app when the user types 'bye'. Tagged as Level-1 increment.

commitResults.messageTitle: feat: mark tasks as done or not done
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a Task class with a done flag, shown as [X] or [ ] in the list.
The 'mark N' command marks task N done and 'unmark N' marks it not done.
Rebuilds the task list (add/list) on top of the Level-1 baseline.
Tagged as Level-4 increment.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add maple package and missing Javadoc
commitResults.messageBody:
All classes live in the default package and some public methods
(e.g. Ui.showWelcome, Task.markDone) have no header comments.

The SE-EDU Java coding standard requires every class to belong to a
package and every public class and method to carry header Javadoc.

Let's move all classes into a single maple package matching the
project name and add the missing Javadoc comments.

Using a single package keeps the change minimal for a project of
this size; subpackages can be introduced later if needed.

Java code in this project must comply with the SE-EDU Java coding
standard (basic + intermediate rules), but no single source of those
rules exists in the repo.

A reusable skill lets any agent check code against the standard
before writing, editing, or reviewing it.

Let's add the seedu-java-coding-standard skill containing the naming,
layout, statement, import, and Javadoc rules from the SE-EDU guide.

Commit messages in this project must follow the SE-EDU Git
conventions on the subject line, body structure, and branch names,
but the rules are currently only referenced from a URL.

A reusable skill keeps the rules available to any agent that writes
or reviews commit messages and tags.

Let's add the seedu-git-standard skill covering the subject format,
the body structure (current situation, why, what), and lightweight
tag usage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mandate SE-EDU coding and Git standards
commitResults.messageBody:
AGENTS.md lists project requirements but does not yet require any
specific code or commit conventions.

Commits so far mix styles and Java code may drift from the SE-EDU
standards without a mandate.

Let's add mandatory sections that require all Java code to follow
the SE-EDU Java coding standard (basic + intermediate) and all
commits to follow the SE-EDU Git conventions, referencing the two
project skills that encode those rules.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Todo, Deadline and Event task types
commitResults.messageBody:
The app only supports a single Task type with no timing information,
so tasks cannot capture due dates or event windows.

Level-4 requires tracking three task types: todos, deadlines and events.

Let's add Todo, Deadline and Event subclasses that inherit from a Task
class, and parse todo, deadline and event commands to create them.

Task type icons are shown in the list so users can tell the types
apart at a glance.

The command loop hard-codes command keywords and substring lengths,
which hurts readability and makes maintenance error-prone.

Let's extract the keywords into constants, delegate each command to a
helper method, and merge the duplicated mark and unmark logic.

This keeps the main loop at a single level of abstraction and removes
magic literals.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle malformed deadline and event commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The deadline and event parsers assume the "/by", "/from" and "/to"
markers are present, so a malformed command throws an
ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of responding gracefully.

Let's check for the required markers before parsing and fall back to
the unknown command message when they are missing.

Detailed error messages for malformed commands arrive with Level-5.
